title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Active and Passive Voice
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct passive voice form of the sentence:
"The mechanic repaired the car."
options: The car is repaired by the mechanic.
The car was repaired by the mechanic.
The car has been repaired by the mechanic.
The car had been repaired by the mechanic.
questions.explain: To change a simple past tense active sentence ('repaired') into the passive voice, use 'was/were' + past participle. The object 'the car' becomes the subject, resulting in 'The car was repaired by the mechanic.'
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which of the following is the correct active voice for the sentence below?
"The letter is being written by Mary."
options: Mary is writing the letter.
Mary was writing the letter.
Mary writes the letter.
Mary has written the letter.
questions.explain: The passive sentence uses 'is being written', which is the present continuous passive. To convert to active, we need the present continuous active verb: 'is writing'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is written in the passive voice?
options: The teacher explained the lesson clearly.
The cake was eaten by the children.
They will buy a new house next year.
She is singing a beautiful song.
questions.explain: In a passive sentence, the subject receives the action (Object + be + Past Participle + by + Subject). In 'The cake was eaten by the children', 'the cake' is the receiver of the action.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Convert the following sentence into the passive voice:
"They must have completed the project by now."
options: The project must be completed by them by now.
The project must have been completed by them by now.
The project has been completed by them by now.
The project had been completed by them by now.
questions.explain: When converting a modal perfect verb (must have + past participle) to the passive voice, the structure is: modal + have been + past participle (must have been completed).
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which of the following is an acceptable passive transformation of the sentence: 
"The principal awarded him a medal."
options: He was awarded a medal by the principal.
A medal is awarded to him by the principal.
The principal was awarded by a medal for him.
He has been awarded a medal by the principal.
questions.explain: This sentence has two objects (him, a medal). It can be made passive by making the indirect object 'him' the subject: 'He was awarded a medal by the principal.' Option B has the wrong tense, and D is present perfect instead of past.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
What is the passive voice form of the following question?
"Who wrote this beautiful poem?"
options: Who was written by this beautiful poem?
By who was this beautiful poem written?
By whom was this beautiful poem written?
Who has written this beautiful poem?
questions.explain: In interrogative sentences starting with 'Who', the passive structure begins with 'By whom', followed by the auxiliary verb ('was'), the subject ('this beautiful poem'), and the past participle ('written').
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the correct passive voice version of the imperative command:
"Shut the door!"
options: The door must shut.
Let the door be shut.
You shut the door.
The door is shut by you.
questions.explain: To change a direct command or imperative sentence into the passive voice, we typically use the formula: Let + object + be + past participle.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the correct passive form of this present continuous active sentence:
"The chef is preparing the meal in the kitchen."
options: The meal is prepared by the chef in the kitchen.
The meal was being prepared by the chef in the kitchen.
The meal is being prepared by the chef in the kitchen.
The meal has been prepared by the chef in the kitchen.
questions.explain: The present continuous passive requires the structure: object + am/is/are + being + past participle. Thus, 'is being prepared' is the correct tense conversion.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
What is the passive form of the following future simple sentence?
"Will they build a new school in our town?"
options: Will a new school be built in our town?
Would a new school be built in our town?
Is a new school built in our town?
Will a new school build in our town?
questions.explain: In an interrogative future simple sentence, the passive structure is: 'Will' + subject ('a new school') + 'be' + past participle ('built').
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the voice of the following sentence:
"The application must be submitted by Friday."
options: Active voice
Passive voice
Direct speech
Indirect speech
questions.explain: The sentence focuses on the action and the receiver (the application) rather than the doer. The structure 'modal + be + past participle' indicates it is in the passive voice.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Convert the following sentence to the passive voice:
"Somebody has stolen my wallet."
options: My wallet is stolen by somebody.
My wallet has been stolen.
My wallet was stolen.
My wallet had been stolen.
questions.explain: The active sentence uses the present perfect tense ('has stolen'). The passive equivalent is 'has/have been' + past participle ('has been stolen'). It is common to omit 'by somebody'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct active form for the sentence below:
"The national anthem was sung beautifully by the choir."
options: The choir sings the national anthem beautifully.
The choir is singing the national anthem beautifully.
The choir sang the national anthem beautifully.
The choir has sung the national anthem beautifully.
questions.explain: The passive phrase 'was sung' indicates the simple past tense. The active voice must therefore use the simple past verb 'sang'.
questions.subject: English Studies
